title: The intersection of sets
competency: Determine the intersection of two sets and use Venn diagrams for union and intersection.

keywords.def: A ∩ B: all elements that belong to both A and B.
A ∪ B: all elements that belong to A or B or both.

en.text: The intersection of A and B, written A ∩ B, is the set of elements that are in both A and B. Check each element of A: is it also in B? If A = {3, 4, 5, 6} and B = {4, 6, 8, 10}, A ∩ B = {4, 6}. If nothing is shared, A ∩ B = { }.

screens.title: In both clubs
screens.ask: Football club {Abel, Bethel, Chala}. Drama club {Bethel, Dawit}. Who is in BOTH clubs?
screens.after:
Football: Abel, Bethel, Chala.
Drama: Bethel, Dawit.
Only Bethel is in both lists.
The members in both sets form the intersection.

screens.title: 1.3.2 The intersection of sets
paras: Definition 1.7: The intersection of A and B, written A ∩ B and read "A intersection B", is the set of all elements in both A and B.
On a Venn diagram, A ∩ B is the shared middle part of the two circles.

screens.title: A = {3, 4, 5, 6}, B = {4, 6, 8, 10}
overlaps: 4 and 6 are in both: A ∩ B = {4, 6}.

screens.title: Find A ∩ B
steps: Check each element of A = {3, 4, 5, 6} in B = {4, 6, 8, 10}.
Keep the ones in both: 4 and 6.

screens.title: Union or intersection? A = {2, 4, 6, 8}, B = {3, 6, 9}
sets: Circle A: 2, 4, 8 and the middle 6. A = {2, 4, 6, 8}.
Circle B: 3, 9 and the middle 6. B = {3, 6, 9}.
overlaps: Only the middle: A ∩ B = {6}. The union is both circles: A ∪ B = {2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9}.

screens.title: More examples
paras: Two more examples from the book.

screens.title: Find A ∩ B: tap each example.
items: A = {a, e, i, o}, B = {a, e, i}
a, e and i are in both; o is only in A. A ∩ B = {a, e, i} = B.
Nothing is shared. A ∩ B = { }, the empty set.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A ∩ B: all elements that belong to both A and B.

screens.text: A = {3, 4, 5, 6} and B = {4, 6, 8, 10}. Tap every element of A ∩ B.
screens.why:
Check each element of A in B = {4, 6, 8, 10}.
3 ∉ B, 4 ∈ B, 5 ∉ B, 6 ∈ B.
Keep only the ones in both: 4 and 6.
A ∩ B = {4, 6}.
8 and 10 are only in B, so leave them.
screens.clue: Keep only the elements in both sets.

screens.text: Find the intersection: A = {4, 7, 9} and B = {a, e, i}. A ∩ B = ?
screens.why:
A holds numbers; B holds letters.
Check 4, 7, 9 in B: none is there.
Nothing is shared.
A ∩ B = { }, the empty set.
{4, 7, 9, a, e, i} would be the union, not the intersection.

screens.text: Find the intersection: A = {1, 3, 4, 6} and B = {1, 4, 3}. A ∩ B = ?
screens.why:
Check each element of A in B.
1 ∈ B, 3 ∈ B, 4 ∈ B.
6 ∉ B.
A ∩ B = {1, 3, 4}.

screens.title: Place each number: A = {2, 5, 7}, B = {5, 7, 9}
screens.why:
Check each number in A and in B.
2 is in A only.
5 and 7 are in both: they go in A ∩ B.
9 is in B only.
So A ∩ B = {5, 7}.
screens.clue: Check each number in both sets.

screens.text: Intersection of a subset: if A ⊂ B, then A ∩ B = ?
screens.why:
A ⊂ B: every element of A is also in B.
So all of A is shared with B.
B's extra elements are not in A, so they are left out.
A ∩ B = A.
screens.clue: Draw A inside B. What part is in both?

screens.text: Two steps: A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}. E = the even numbers in A. M = {3, 6, 9}. Tap every element of E ∩ M.
screens.why:
First find E: the even numbers in A are 2, 4, 6.
So E = {2, 4, 6}.
Check each in M = {3, 6, 9}: 2 ∉ M, 4 ∉ M, 6 ∈ M.
E ∩ M = {6}.
3 and 9 are in M, but they are not even.
screens.clue: Write E first. Then keep what is also in M.

screens.title: ∈ and ∉
steps: A set lists its elements between braces: A = {3, 4, 5}.
3 ∈ A means 3 is an element of A.
8 ∉ A means 8 is not an element of A.

screens.text: Element or not: A = {3, 4, 5}. Which statement is true?
screens.why:
A = {3, 4, 5}: look between the braces.
4 and 5 are listed, so 4 ∉ A is false.
8 is not listed, so 8 ∈ A is false.
5 is listed, so 5 ∈ A is true.

items.why:
Check each element of A in B = {1, 4, 3}.
1, 3 and 4 are in B.
6 ∉ B.
A ∩ B = {1, 3, 4}.
items.clue: Check each element of A in B.

items.why:
C = { } has no element.
So nothing can be in both A and C.
A ∩ C = { }.

Check each element of A in D.
1, 3, 4 and 6 are all in D.
So A ∩ D = A = {1, 3, 4, 6}.
2 and 5 are only in D.
items.clue: Check each element of A in D.

items.why:
Write A: 1, 3, 4, 6.
B = {1, 4, 3}: all already written.
B adds nothing new.
A ∪ B = {1, 3, 4, 6}.
items.clue: List A, then add new elements of B.

items.why:
C = { } has no element.
It adds nothing to B.
C ∪ B = B = {1, 3, 4}.
items.clue: The empty set adds no element.

items.why:
Write D: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.
B = {1, 4, 3}: all already in D.
So B adds nothing.
B ∪ D = D = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}.
items.clue: Does B add anything new to D?

items.why:
Bracket first: A ∩ B = {1, 3, 4}.
Then join with C = { }.
The empty set adds nothing.
(A ∩ B) ∪ C = {1, 3, 4}.

Bracket first: B ∪ C = {1, 3, 4} ∪ { } = {1, 3, 4}.
Then keep what is also in D.
1, 3 and 4 are all in D.
(B ∪ C) ∩ D = {1, 3, 4}.

First bracket: A ∩ B = {1, 3, 4}.
Second bracket: B ∩ D = {1, 3, 4}, since B ⊆ D.
Join them: {1, 3, 4} ∪ {1, 3, 4}.
The answer is {1, 3, 4}. 6 is not in B, so it is left out.

items.text: Venn diagram: 5 and 7 only in A; 2 in the middle; 3 and 1 only in B. Read the diagram: tap every element of set A.
items.why:
Set A is everything inside circle A.
That is the part only in A: 5 and 7.
Plus the middle part, which is inside A too: 2.
A = {2, 5, 7}.

items.text: Venn diagram: 5 and 7 only in A; 2 in the middle; 3 and 1 only in B. Read the diagram: tap every element of set B.
items.why:
Set B is everything inside circle B.
The part only in B: 3 and 1.
Plus the middle part: 2.
B = {1, 2, 3}.

items.text: Venn diagram: 5 and 7 only in A; 2 in the middle; 3 and 1 only in B. Read the diagram: A ∩ B = ?
items.why:
A ∩ B is the part inside both circles.
That is the middle part.
Only 2 is there.
A ∩ B = {2}. {5, 7} is the part only in A.
items.clue: Which part is in both circles?

items.text: Venn diagram: 5 and 7 only in A; 2 in the middle; 3 and 1 only in B. Read the diagram: tap every element of A ∪ B.
items.why:
A ∪ B is everything inside either circle.
Only A: 5, 7. Middle: 2. Only B: 3, 1.
A ∪ B = {1, 2, 3, 5, 7}.
9 is not in the diagram.

items.text: Union of a subset: if A ⊂ B, then A ∪ B = ?
items.why:
A ⊂ B: circle A is inside circle B.
Every element of A is already in B.
So A adds nothing to B.
A ∪ B = B.

test.text: Find the intersection: A = {2, 4, 6, 8} and B = {4, 8, 12}. Tap every element of A ∩ B.
test.why:
Check each element of A in B = {4, 8, 12}.
2 ∉ B, 4 ∈ B, 6 ∉ B, 8 ∈ B.
A ∩ B = {4, 8}.
12 is only in B.

test.text: Find the intersection: A = {a, b} and B = {c, d}. A ∩ B = ?
test.why:
Check a and b in B = {c, d}.
Neither is there.
Nothing is shared, so A ∩ B = { }.
{a, b, c, d} is A ∪ B, not A ∩ B.

test.text: Intersection of a subset: if A ⊆ B, which is always true?
test.why:
A ⊆ B: every element of A is in B.
So all of A is shared: A ∩ B = A.
A ∩ B = B fails when B has extra elements.
A ∪ B = A also fails then; in fact A ∪ B = B.

test.ask: Count the intersection: A = {1, 2, 3, 4} and B = {3, 4, 5}. A ∩ B has ___ elements.
test.why:
Check each element of A in B.
1 ∉ B, 2 ∉ B, 3 ∈ B, 4 ∈ B.
A ∩ B = {3, 4}.
It has 2 elements.

test.ask: Two steps: A = {1, 2, 3} and B = {2, 3, 4}. (A ∩ B) ∪ {5} has ___ elements.
test.why:
Bracket first: A ∩ B = {2, 3}.
Join with {5}: {2, 3} ∪ {5} = {2, 3, 5}.
Count: 3 elements.

notes.text: Examples 4 and 5 write "A = {a, e, i}" for the second set; it should be B. Shown as B.

Exercise 1.3.1 Q3 (shade A ∩ B) has no diagram of its own; left out. Q4's picture labels A on the outer circle, but the question says A ⊂ B; the items use A ⊂ B as written.
